mainTopic: Does a שינוי (change) cancel an item's status? בית שמאי and בית הלל on a changed אתנן, אביי's list of תנאים, רבא's rejections, and שמואל's ruling about a stolen animal that got weaker
overview: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא in which בית שמאי forbid a changed אתנן for the מזבח and בית הלל permit it. Each side reads a different word in the same פסוק: 'גם' includes changed forms, and 'הם' excludes them. The word 'גם' stays a קשיא against בית הלל. Next the גמרא finds the sources for the other תנאים on אביי's list who hold that a שינוי does not change an item's status: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב (a ברכה on bread baked from stolen wheat), רבי שמעון בן אלעזר (a robber's improvements, explained by רב ששת and by תקנת השבים), and רבי ישמעאל (פאה given even from dough). רב פפא asks why so many תנאים would follow בית שמאי, and אביי answers that on this point even בית הלל agree. רבא then rejects every proof, showing that each case has its own special reason. רבי יונתן's question and the extra word 'תעזב' back up רבא's point about רבי ישמעאל. Finally, שמואל rules like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The גמרא settles the clash with שמואל's other ruling according to רבא, and for אביי it begins quoting a different version of שמואל's words, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בית שמאי forbid and בית הלל permit a changed harlot's payment
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא taught by גוריון of אספורק records a מחלוקת: בית שמאי forbid offering a changed אתנן, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Taught by גוריון) of אספורק: בית שמאי forbid it, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a teaching that settles which way to rule on a changed אתנן: it is a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is an אתנן, such as wheat, olives or grapes, that was turned into flour, oil or wine. בית שמאי say it is still forbidden for the מזבח. בית הלל say the change makes it permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A payment given to a harlot; it may not be brought as a קרבן
They forbid
They permit
A change in the item's form (wheat into flour, grapes into wine)

phrases.english: of Asporak:
Beit Shammai prohibit,
and Beit Hillel permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹסְרִין, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא the גמרא was quoting before this section began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A changed אתנן: בית שמאי forbid it for the מזבח, and בית הלל permit it.

steps.title: What is בית שמאי's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind בית שמאי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where בית שמאי get the idea that a changed אתנן is still forbidden. This sets up the next step, which finds a source for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The natural assumption is that a big change, like grapes into wine, makes the item 'new.' So the גמרא wants to know what pushes בית שמאי to forbid it anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his (their) reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Beit Shammai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for בית שמאי forbidding a changed אתנן.

steps.title: Each side reads a different word in the verse
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי learn from 'גם שניהם' that changed items are included. בית הלל learn from 'הם' that changed items are excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'even both of them,' which comes to include their changed forms. And בית הלל: the פסוק says 'them,' meaning them and not their changed forms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by showing that both sides learn from the same פסוק. Each side focuses on a different word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'גם' (also/even) is read as adding something extra, so בית שמאי include the changed forms. The word 'הם' (them) is read as narrowing, meaning only these items exactly as they are, so בית הלל exclude the changed forms.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Also/even', a word that includes something extra (ריבוי)
To include
'Them', a word that narrows (מיעוט)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the section: each side now has to explain the word the other side relies on.

phrases.english: The verse states: "even both of them"
– to include their changed forms.
And Beit Hillel – the verse states: "them"
– and not their changed forms.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about בית שמאי, and also gives בית הלל's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי: 'גם' includes changed forms. בית הלל: 'הם' excludes them.

steps.title: What do בית שמאי do with the word 'them'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges בית שמאי: the פסוק also says 'הם,' which seems to exclude changed forms.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for בית שמאי, isn't 'them' written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בית שמאי with בית הלל's word. If 'הם' narrows the rule, why don't בית שמאי exclude changed items?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה must teach something. If בית שמאי ignore 'הם,' they are leaving a word unexplained. They also seem to contradict their own ריבוי from 'גם.'

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written!

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai, isn't "them" written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests בית שמאי against the word בית הלל used.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's reading of the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'הם' is a narrowing word. בית שמאי must account for it, and it seems to exclude changed forms.

steps.title: For בית שמאי, 'them' excludes offspring
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי use 'הם' for a different exclusion: the offspring of an animal given as אתנן are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed for: 'them,' and not their offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בית שמאי do use the word 'הם,' but for a different purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בית שמאי, 'הם' teaches that the animal itself is forbidden, but its babies are not. So the word is not wasted, and it does not clash with including changed forms.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for another teaching)
Their offspring

phrases.english: That one is needed by him for:
"them" – and not their offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא on בית שמאי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the word to a different teaching
steps.terutzMaskana: For בית שמאי, 'הם' excludes offspring, not changed forms.

steps.title: בית הלל learn two things from 'them'
steps.stepSummary: How do בית הלל know offspring are excluded? They learn both exclusions from the one word 'הם.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל? You learn two things from it: 'them' and not their changed forms, 'them' and not their offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how בית הלל know that offspring are permitted, since they already used 'הם' for changed forms. It answers that the one word teaches both rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל read 'הם' as a broad narrowing: only the original item itself is forbidden. That rules out both its changed form and its offspring, so no second source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: You learn two things from it

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel – you learn two things from it.
phrases.notes: 'And בית הלל' is a short question: where do they learn the offspring rule from? The rest is the answer.

phrases.english: "Them" and not their changed forms,
"them" and not their offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to בית הלל, who need a source for the offspring rule that בית שמאי just took from 'הם.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One word, 'הם,' teaches both exclusions for בית הלל.

steps.title: What do בית הלל do with the word 'even'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges בית הלל: the פסוק also says 'גם,' which seems to include changed forms.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for בית הלל too, isn't 'even' written?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns the challenge around. It asks בית הלל how they explain the word 'גם' that בית שמאי rely on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'גם' is an including word. If בית הלל don't use it to include changed forms, what does it come to add?

keyTerms.meaning: Also / too

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel too, isn't "even" written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 4: now the other side must explain the opposing word.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's reading of the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'גם' is an including word. בית הלל leave it unexplained, and it seems to include changed forms.

steps.title: The word 'even' remains a difficulty for בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits it has no answer: 'גם' is a difficulty for בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Even' is difficult for בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not answer the challenge. It openly admits that the word 'גם' remains a problem for בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike בית שמאי, who found a use for 'הם,' בית הלל are left without an explanation for 'גם.' The word 'קשיא' marks a difficulty that is left standing. It does not cancel בית הלל's opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult (a question left unanswered)

steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' here does not mean בית הלל's view is rejected. It just means the גמרא could not explain one word according to them.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: 'גם' includes changed forms, and 'הם' excludes offspring. בית הלל: 'הם' excludes both changed forms and offspring, but 'גם' stays a difficulty for them.

phrases.english: "Even" is difficult for Beit Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Admits the challenge from step 7 has no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The word 'גם' remains an unresolved difficulty for בית הלל.

steps.title: What is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question: what is the source or teaching of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is (the teaching of) רבי אליעזר בן יעקב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new topic. It asks about רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's teaching, which it will explain next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב was mentioned earlier in the sugya as holding that a changed item keeps its old status. Now the גמרא wants to see exactly where his view is found.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (What does this refer to?)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב מַאי הִיא?
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov, what is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues identifying, one by one, the sources for the תנאים on אביי's list. בית שמאי's source was just explained, and now the גמרא turns to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The teaching of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב that the sugya referred to.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: Baking Stolen Wheat Doesn't Make It Yours
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds that stolen wheat is still stolen even after it is ground, kneaded, and baked.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, if someone stole a סאה of wheat, ground it, kneaded it, baked it, and then separated חלה from it, how can he say a ברכה? He is not blessing. He is insulting ה׳! About him the פסוק says: 'The robber who blesses insults ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9 by quoting a ברייתא from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. A robber who bakes stolen wheat and then separates חלה is not blessing; he is insulting ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grinding, kneading, and baking are big changes to the wheat. If such a שינוי made the wheat his, his ברכה would be fine. Since רבי אליעזר בן יעקב calls the ברכה an insult, he must hold the bread is still stolen, so a שינוי does not take away the owner's ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of volume (here, an amount of wheat)
The portion of dough separated and given to a כהן
Insults or disgraces (ה׳)
A robber, one who takes what isn't his
A change in the item's form

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says 'a שינוי doesn't acquire' in words. The גמרא learns it from the fact that the ברכה is called an insult. That only makes sense if the bread is still stolen.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
Here is one who robbed a se'a of wheat,
ground it, kneaded it, and baked it,
and separated challah from it,
how can he recite a blessing?
This one is not blessing, but rather insulting [ה׳]!
And about this it is said:
"The robber who blesses insults ה׳."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 by quoting the ברייתא that is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא: a robber's ברכה over חלה from stolen wheat he baked is an insult, so the changed wheat is still stolen.

steps.title: What Is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's Source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we see רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the source for רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the source of a second תנא, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. This line sets up the next step, where a ברייתא will be quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question that was asked about רבי אליעזר בן יעקב in step 9. The גמרא wants to see where רבי שמעון בן אלעזר shows that a changed item keeps its old status.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (What is his source or teaching?)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר מַאי הִיא?
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, what is it?
phrases.notes: He means: what source shows us רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 9, now asked about a second תנא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view on a changed item.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's Rule About a Robber's Improvements
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: when a robber improves a stolen item, the robber has the upper hand. He can take payment for his improvement or say 'here is yours.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר stated this rule: for any improvement a robber made, he has the upper hand. If he wants, he takes payment for his improvement. If he wants, he says to the owner, 'Here is yours in front of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule. A robber who improved the stolen item has the upper hand: he may take his improvement or say 'here is yours in front of you.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'here is yours in front of you' means the item never stopped being the owner's, even after it changed. The wording is unclear, though. Why would a robber who could be paid for his improvement ever give that up? The next step will ask exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: Improvement, added value
A robber
He has the upper hand (the better side of the deal)
Here is yours in front of you (take your item as it is)

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, כְּלָל זֶה אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: this rule was stated by Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar:
Any improvement that a robber made,
he has the upper hand.
If he wants, he takes [payment for] his improvement,
if he wants, he says to him: "Here is yours in front of you."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, כְּלָל זֶה אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by quoting רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא about a robber's improvements, which shows the item can be returned as the owner's.

steps.title: The Wording Doesn't Make Sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is puzzled. Why would a robber who could be paid for his improvement ever choose to just give the item back?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the ברייתא's wording is confusing. This sets up רב ששת's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes it sound like the robber picks between two choices for the same improved item. But if he can be paid for the improvement, giving it back for nothing is never a real choice. So the plain reading seems not to work.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? (The wording seems not to make sense)

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how to read the ברייתא quoted in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'if he wants... if he wants' wording of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A robber who can be paid for his improvement would never choose to give it back for free, so the two 'choices' make no sense.

steps.title: רב ששת: Two Different Cases
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the ברייתא is talking about two separate cases. If the robber improved the item, he is paid for it. If the item got worse, he just returns it, because a שינוי does not change ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said, this is what he means: if he improved it, he takes payment for his improvement. If it got worse, he says to the owner, 'Here is yours in front of you,' because the changed item stays in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת explains that the ברייתא is not offering two choices. It describes two cases: an item that got better, and an item that got worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because 'a שינוי stays in its place,' the item still belongs to the owner even after it changed. So if it got worse, the robber returns it as it is and owes nothing more. This is why רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is a source that a שינוי does not acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means
Got weaker, lost value
A change leaves the item where it was (ownership does not change)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said, this is what he is saying:
[If] he improved it, he takes [payment for] his improvement.
[If] it got worse, he says to him: "Here is yours in front of you,"
because a change stays in its place.
phrases.notes: The change doesn't move the item into the robber's ownership. It's still the owner's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the puzzle of step 13 by splitting the ברייתא into two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the ברייתא as two separate cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא gives the robber a choice for the same improved item.
steps.terutzMaskana: Improved item: the robber is paid for the improvement. Worsened item: he returns it as is, because a שינוי does not change ownership.

steps.title: Then Why Pay Him for Improvements?
steps.stepSummary: If a שינוי does not change ownership, then even an improved item should simply go back to the owner, and the robber should get nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even if he improved it, it should be the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת. If the item always stays the owner's, the robber should not be paid even when he improved it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's reason ('a שינוי stays in its place') means the owner owns the item, improvement and all. So paying the robber for the improvement seems to go against his own reason.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Even ... also (the same rule should apply here too)

phrases.english: If so, even [if] he improved it, also [it should be the owner's]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's explanation from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling that an improving robber is paid for his improvement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a שינוי doesn't change ownership, the improved item and its improvement belong to the owner, so the robber deserves nothing.

steps.title: Because of the Rule to Help Robbers Do תשובה
steps.stepSummary: Paying the robber for improvements comes from תקנת השבים, a rule חז"ל made so that robbers who want to do תשובה won't be held back.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: it is because of the rule made for people doing תשובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that by strict law the robber would get nothing. חז"ל made a rule to pay him for his improvements so he won't be held back from returning the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic law stays the same: a שינוי does not change ownership. The payment for improvements is a separate rule added by חז"ל, not part of the basic law. Without it, a robber might keep the stolen item instead of returning it.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule made by חז"ל to help people who want to do תשובה (return what they stole)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, a changed stolen item still belongs to the owner. A robber is paid for improvements only because of תקנת השבים, not because the change made the item his.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the difference between the basic law and a rule added by חז"ל: the robber's payment for improvements is a special exception, while the basic rule about שינוי stays in place.

phrases.english: They say: because of the ordinance for the penitent.
phrases.notes: The 'penitent' are robbers who want to do תשובה and give back what they stole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A rule added by חז"ל explains the exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Paying for improvements contradicts the idea that a שינוי doesn't change ownership.
steps.terutzMaskana: By strict law the robber gets nothing. חז"ל gave him payment for improvements so robbers won't be held back from doing תשובה.

steps.title: What is רבי ישמעאל's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we see that רבי ישמעאל holds a שינוי does not change an item's status.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the source for רבי ישמעאל?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי had included רבי ישמעאל in his list of תנאים, and now the גמרא asks where his view appears. This question sets up the next step, where the source is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name on אביי's list needs a real source behind it. This line simply asks for the one belonging to רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? A request to name the source being referred to

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, what is [his source]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues identifying, one by one, the sources for the תנאים אביי listed before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which teaching shows that רבי ישמעאל holds a שינוי leaves the item's status in place.

steps.title: פאה must be given even from dough
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the stages at which פאה can be separated. רבי ישמעאל adds that it can be separated even after the grain has become dough.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: The ideal way to do the מצוה of פאה is to separate it from the standing grain. If he did not separate it from the standing grain, he separates it from the sheaves. If he did not separate it from the sheaves, he separates it from the pile, as long as he has not smoothed the pile. If he smoothed it, he takes מעשר first and then gives the poor their share. In the name of רבי ישמעאל they said: he may even separate it from the dough and give it to the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא about פאה, the corner of the field that belongs to the poor. רבי ישמעאל says the obligation remains even after the grain has been turned into dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain ground and kneaded into dough has gone through a major change. Yet according to רבי ישמעאל, the dough still carries the פאה obligation of the original grain. This shows he holds that a שינוי does not change the item's status.

keyTerms.meaning: The corner of the field that must be left for the poor
Standing grain that has not yet been harvested
Sheaves, meaning bundles of harvested grain
A pile of threshed grain
He smoothed the pile. This final step makes the grain obligated in מַעֲשֵׂר
Dough

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ישמעאל, פאה must be given even from dough. The change from grain to dough does not cancel the obligation, which is why אביי lists him.

phrases.english: As it was taught: The מצוה of pe'a
phrases.notes: He means the best, ideal way to do the מצוה.

phrases.english: is to separate it from the standing grain.
If he did not separate it from the standing grain,
he separates it from the sheaves.
If he did not separate it from the sheaves,

phrases.aramaic: מַפְרִישׁ מִן הַכְּרִי עַד שֶׁלֹּא מֵרְחוֹ.
phrases.english: he separates it from the pile, as long as he has not smoothed it.
If he smoothed it, he tithes and then gives to him.
phrases.notes: Smoothing the pile makes the grain obligated in מעשר, so he tithes first. "Him" means the poor person.

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Yishmael they said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַפְרִישׁ מִן הָעִיסָּה וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ.
phrases.english: He may even separate from the dough and give it to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 by quoting the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי ישמעאל requires פאה to be given even from dough. A grain that went through a major change keeps its פאה obligation.

steps.title: Would all these תנאים follow בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי why so many תנאים would go to such effort to teach a view that matches בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Did all these תנאים go to such trouble just to teach us a law that follows בית שמאי?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the purpose of אביי's whole list. The rule that a שינוי does not change status is known as בית שמאי's view, and we normally follow בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule belongs only to בית שמאי, it would be strange for so many תנאים to keep teaching it. רב פפא is asking whether אביי's list really establishes a rule we can rely on.

keyTerms.meaning: Did they go to the trouble? Did they make such an effort?
The school of שמאי. The הלכה usually does not follow them when they argue with בית הלל

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Did all these tannaim go to the trouble
to teach us [a law] like Beit Shammai?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכְּפוּל כֹּל הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי לְאַשְׁמוֹעִינַן כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the list now complete, רב פפא challenges what the list accomplishes.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's list of תנאים who hold that a שינוי does not change status.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule is בית שמאי's view, which we usually do not follow, so it makes little sense for many תנאים to keep teaching it.

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל agree on this
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the תנאים are teaching that, in these cases, בית הלל agrees with בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what they are saying: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not disagree about this matter.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains the purpose of all these תנאים. They hold that in these cases there is no argument at all, so even בית הלל agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנאים are not siding with a minority view. They are teaching that the rule is agreed upon in the cases they discuss, so it carries real halachic weight.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what they are saying. It introduces a new reading of their point
They did not disagree
The school of הלל. The הלכה usually follows them

steps.whyThisMatters: With this answer, אביי's list becomes evidence for a rule that is agreed upon, not just one side of a debate.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what they are saying:
phrases.notes: אביי is answering. "They" means all the תנאים on his list.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל בְּדָבָר זֶה.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree about this matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמְרִי: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל בְּדָבָר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the purpose of the sources
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים were simply repeating בית שמאי's minority view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנאים are teaching that in these cases even בית הלל agrees that a שינוי does not change status.

steps.title: רבא: maybe the case is only about removable dye
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins to question the proof from רבי שמעון בן יהודה. His case may be only about dye, which can be washed out with soap, so it may not count as a real change.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do you know this? Perhaps רבי שמעון בן יהודה said his ruling there only about dye, since it can be removed with soap.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts rejecting the proofs on אביי's list, beginning with רבי שמעון בן יהודה. He goes on to the other cases in steps 22-26.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dyeing wool is a change that can be undone, because soap washes the dye out. So רבי שמעון בן יהודה may hold that the wool keeps its status only because the change is reversible, not because every שינוי leaves the status in place.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this? A request for proof
Perhaps. It introduces another possible explanation
Dye
A soap-like cleaning substance

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the dyed wool lost its status. He is saying it keeps its status for a narrower reason, because the change can be undone, and that reason may not apply to every שינוי.

phrases.english: Rava said: From where [is this proven]?
Perhaps he only said [his ruling]
Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda, there,
phrases.notes: "There" is his earlier case: the first shearing of wool (ראשית הגז) that was dyed.

phrases.english: only regarding dye, since one can remove it
by means of soap;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the question of whose view this is to whether the sources prove the rule at all.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי שמעון בן יהודה, the first of several sources רבא will question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Dye is a reversible change, so his ruling may rest on that fact and not on a general rule about every שינוי.

steps.title: בית שמאי may only be talking about offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבא says בית שמאי may hold that a change does not help only for items brought to the מזבח, because an item used as payment to a prostitute has become disgusting for holy use.
steps.simpleTranslation: And maybe בית שמאי only said their view there about items for the Most High, because the item has become repulsive.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the proof from בית שמאי. He says their rule may apply only to offerings for the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof assumed that בית שמאי think a change never matters. רבא suggests a narrower reason: something given as a prostitute's fee is disgusting for holy use, even after it changes form. So this case teaches nothing about ordinary halachic matters like stolen property.

keyTerms.meaning: They only said their view in this specific case (a formula that limits a ruling to its own situation)
The school of שמאי
For the Most High, meaning for offerings on the מזבח
It has become repulsive or disgusting

phrases.english: And maybe they only said
בית שמאי, there,
phrases.notes: This goes back to their case of a prostitute paid with wheat that was later ground into flour.

phrases.english: only regarding the Most High
because it has become repulsive;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's series of rejections that began with רבי שמעון בן יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Their ruling may depend on the item being disgusting for holy use, not on a general rule that a change does not matter

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב may only be talking about a blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי אליעזר בן יעקב may only mean that a thief cannot make a ברכה on stolen wheat, because that would be a מצוה הבאה בעבירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And maybe רבי אליעזר בן יעקב only said his view there about a blessing, because it is a מצוה that comes through a sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the proof from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. He says that case is only about making a ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case was about a thief who turned stolen wheat into bread and then blessed on it. Blessing is not allowed because it is a מצוה הבאה בעבירה, a מצוה done through a sin. That reason stands even if the change gives him ownership, so it proves nothing about ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: A blessing
A מצוה done by means of a sin, which is not acceptable

phrases.english: And maybe he only said
רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, there,
only regarding a blessing
because it is
a מצוה that comes through a sin;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next rejection in the same series
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ban on blessing comes from the rule of מצוה הבאה בעבירה, not from the item staying stolen

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר may only be talking about weakening that can be reversed
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's case is about an animal that got weak, which can be undone, so it is not a real change.
steps.simpleTranslation: And maybe רבי שמעון בן אלעזר only said his view there about weakening that goes back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the proof from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. He says that case is about a weakening that can be reversed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that has become thin can be fattened up again. So it was never truly changed. That says nothing about a permanent change, like wheat turned into flour.

keyTerms.meaning: Weakening or thinning of an animal
That returns, meaning it can be reversed

phrases.english: And maybe he only said
רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, there,
only regarding weakening that goes back;
phrases.notes: The animal can be fattened again, so the weakness is only temporary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next rejection in the same series
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A reversible change is not a real שינוי, so the case does not show that a permanent change has no effect

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל may only be talking about פאה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי ישמעאל's ruling that פאה can be given even from dough comes from an extra word in the תורה, so it applies only to פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And maybe רבי ישמעאל only said his view there about פאה, because the word "you shall leave" is written an extra time!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the proof from רבי ישמעאל (Step 18). He says that ruling comes from a special extra word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תעזב appears twice about the poor, so one is extra. That extra word teaches that פאה must be given in every situation, even after the grain became dough. So the rule is a special law of פאה, not a general rule about changes.

keyTerms.meaning: The corner of the field left for the poor
As it is written
You shall leave (them for the poor)
Extra, written more times than needed

phrases.english: And maybe he only said
רבי ישמעאל, there,
only regarding פאה
because "you shall leave" is written an extra time!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:10 and ויקרא 23:22. Since the word appears twice, one of them is extra.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next rejection in the same series, now aimed at the main proof for רבי ישמעאל
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי ישמעאל's ruling on פאה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His ruling comes from an extra word in the פסוק that is limited to פאה

steps.title: No general rule can be learned from gifts to the poor
steps.stepSummary: רבא blocks the idea of using פאה as a model for other laws, because מתנות עניים are a special category.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: let us learn from it to other laws. Gifts to the poor are different!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא expects someone to say, "Fine, but let us learn from פאה to other areas." He answers that gifts to the poor are special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might argue that once the פסוק teaches that a change does not matter for פאה, we can apply this to other laws. רבא answers that מתנות עניים have their own special rules, so they cannot be a source for other laws. With this, all the proofs about רבי ישמעאל have been rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introducing an expected objection)
Let us learn from it
Gifts to the poor, such as פאה
Is different

steps.whatToRemember: רבא showed that every proof has its own special reason: dye that can be washed out (רבי שמעון בן יהודה), offerings (בית שמאי), a blessing through a sin (רבי אליעזר בן יעקב), reversible weakening (רבי שמעון בן אלעזר), and an extra פסוק about gifts to the poor (רבי ישמעאל). So none of them proves a general rule that a שינוי does not change an item's status.

phrases.english: And if you will say: let us learn from it,
phrases.notes: He means learning from פאה that a change does not matter in other areas of halacha too.

phrases.english: gifts to the poor are different!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ahead of time an objection to Step 25 and finishes רבא's series of rejections
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Any attempt to learn a general rule from פאה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: מתנות עניים are a unique category and cannot serve as a model for other laws

steps.title: רבי יונתן Asked the Same Question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבא's doubt about רבי ישמעאל matches a question already asked by רבי יונתן: is רבי ישמעאל's reason a general rule that שינוי does not acquire, or is it just the extra word תַּעֲזֹב?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the question of רבי יונתן. רבי יונתן asked: What is רבי ישמעאל's reason? Is it because he holds that a change does not give ownership? Or maybe in general he holds that a change does give ownership, and here it is different because the word "you shall leave" is written an extra time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רבא's last answer by showing that רבי יונתן had the very same doubt about רבי ישמעאל's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25, רבא said רבי ישמעאל's ruling might come only from an extra word in the תורה. Here we see that רבי יונתן already raised this as an open question. If it was unclear to רבי יונתן, nobody can use רבי ישמעאל as a firm proof that שינוי אינו קונה.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked a question that he could not settle
A change in the stolen item gives the thief ownership
In general, in all other cases
"You shall leave", the תורה's command about gifts to the poor
Extra, more than needed

phrases.english: This is like the question of Rabbi Yonatan
for Rabbi Yonatan asked:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yishmael?
Is it because he holds that a change does not give ownership?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, בְּעָלְמָא קָסָבַר שִׁינּוּי קוֹנֶה;
phrases.english: Or perhaps in general he holds that a change does give ownership,
and here it is because "you shall leave" is written an extra time?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רבא's rejection in steps 25-26 by showing an earlier אמורא had the same doubt.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that רבי ישמעאל's ruling may be based only on the extra word and not on a general rule
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יונתן's unresolved question about the reason behind רבי ישמעאל's view

steps.title: What Is the Extra Word For?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if רבי ישמעאל's reason is a general rule that שינוי does not acquire, why does the תורה need the extra תַּעֲזֹב? And according to the רבנן, who do not allow פאה from dough, what is it for?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that רבי ישמעאל's reason is that he holds a change does not give ownership, why do I need the extra "you shall leave" that the תורה wrote? And also, according to the רבנן, why do I need the extra "you shall leave" that the תורה wrote?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first side of the question: if nobody needs the extra word for the law of dough, then what is it teaching?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not waste words, so every extra word must teach something. If רבי ישמעאל would allow פאה from dough even without the extra word, the word seems useless to him. The רבנן do not use it for dough at all, so it seems useless to them too.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Why do I need it? (a question about an extra source)
And furthermore
The Sages who argue with רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: And if you will say
that the reason of Rabbi Yishmael
is because he holds that a change does not give ownership,
why do I need the extra "you shall leave" that the Merciful One wrote?
And furthermore, according to the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: These are the Sages who say you cannot give פאה from dough.

phrases.english: why do I need the extra "you shall leave" that the Merciful One wrote?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first option in רבי יונתן's question by asking what the extra word would be for.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the extra תַּעֲזֹב is not needed for dough, either according to רבי ישמעאל (first option) or according to the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every extra word in the תורה must teach something. If it is not needed for dough, it seems to have no purpose.

steps.title: The Extra Word Teaches About an Ownerless Vineyard
steps.stepSummary: The extra תַּעֲזֹב teaches a ברייתא: a person who made his vineyard ownerless and then harvested it early himself must still give the four gifts to the poor, but he does not have to give מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what is taught in a ברייתא: One who made his vineyard ownerless, then got up early in the morning and harvested it, must give פרט, עוללות, שכחה and פאה, but he does not have to give מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra word has its own job: it teaches a law about a vineyard that was made ownerless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually ownerless produce (הפקר) does not need gifts, and that is why he does not give מעשר. The extra תַּעֲזֹב teaches that the gifts to the poor still apply here. So the word is used up on this law, and the question from step 28 goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different teaching)
One who makes his property ownerless (הפקר)
Single grapes that fell during harvest, left for the poor
Small, poorly formed grape clusters, left for the poor
Forgotten clusters, left for the poor
Tithes, a tenth of the produce

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two laws: the gifts to the poor still apply to this ownerless vineyard, but מעשר does not.
steps.whatToRemember: The extra תַּעֲזֹב is used for the ownerless vineyard. So רבי ישמעאל can hold שינוי אינו קונה in general and still have a use for the word, and רבא's point stays open: we cannot prove anything from him.

phrases.english: It is needed for that which is taught in a baraita:
One who made his vineyard ownerless,
and got up early in the morning and harvested it,
is obligated in fallen single grapes and in small clusters
and in forgotten clusters and in pe'a,
but he is exempt from tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 28 by giving the extra word a different job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra תַּעֲזֹב seemed to have no purpose unless it teaches פאה from dough
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra תַּעֲזֹב teaches that the gifts to the poor apply even to a vineyard that was made ownerless and then harvested by its former owner

steps.title: The הלכה Follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main topic of a stolen item that changed, and brings a ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's case, from steps 12-14, is a stolen animal that got weak. In that case the robber returns the animal as it is now, because a שינוי stays in its place. רבא limited this to weakening that can go back (step 24), and that limit will matter in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The final ruling follows (this opinion)

steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the sugya from asking what each תנא holds to what the practical הלכה is for a stolen item that changed.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side question about פאה and returns to the main topic of a stolen item that changed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: a stolen animal that got weak is returned to the owner as it is now.

steps.title: Did שמואל really say that? His other ruling seems to clash
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's ruling like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Elsewhere שמואל said that we do not appraise the change for a thief or a robber, only for damages.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did שמואל really say this? But שמואל said: we do not appraise, not for a thief and not for a robber, only for damages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised at the ruling from step 30. It quotes a different statement of שמואל that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that a thief can return a changed or weakened animal as it is. שמואל's other statement says we do not appraise the loss for a thief or robber, so the thief cannot just hand back the weakened animal and pay the difference. The two statements of שמואל seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And did he really say…?' This opens a challenge to a quoted ruling.
We do not appraise the change in value of the item.
A thief who takes in secret.
A robber who takes openly, by force.
Damages. Someone who has to pay for harm he caused.

phrases.english: But did Shmuel really say this?!
But didn't Shmuel say:
We do not appraise, not for a thief
phrases.notes: 'Appraise' means working out how much value was lost, so he could return the item and just pay the difference.

phrases.english: and not for a robber;
only for damages.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 30 by setting another statement of the same אמורא against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל cannot both let the thief return the changed item as is and also say we never appraise for a thief.

steps.title: According to רבא, the two statements deal with different kinds of weakening
steps.stepSummary: For רבא there is no contradiction. The ruling like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is about weakening that goes back, and 'we do not appraise for a thief' is about weakening that does not go back.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבא, who said that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר spoke only about weakening that goes back. So there is no difficulty. When שמואל says the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, that a change stays in its place, he means weakening that goes back. When שמואל says there that we do not appraise for a thief or a robber, only for damages, he means weakening that does not go back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that according to רבא's earlier explanation of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, the two statements of שמואל fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said רבי שמעון בן אלעזר allows returning the animal as is only when the weakening can go back. So the two rulings of שמואל cover different cases. If the weakening can go back, the thief returns the animal as is. If it cannot go back, we do not appraise, and the thief cannot just pay the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It works well for…' The גמרא admits one view has no problem before it challenges the other view.
Weakening or loss of condition, for example an animal that got thin.
That goes back, meaning reversible.
A change stays in its place. The item is returned as it is now.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key idea of the sugya: whether the weakening can go back decides whether the thief may return the item as is.

phrases.english: It works well according to Rava, who said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר הָתָם –
phrases.english: when Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said it there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's own ברייתא about a robber and the stolen animal (step 12).

phrases.english: it was about weakening that goes back.
So it is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָאָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: when he says the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,
that a change stays in its place,
it is about weakening that goes back;
and when Shmuel says there:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שָׁמִין לֹא לְגַנָּב וְלֹא לְגַזְלָן,
phrases.english: we do not appraise, not for a thief and not for a robber,
only for damages,
it is about weakening that does not go back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31, but only according to רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each statement deals with a different kind of weakening.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements of שמואל seemed to speak about the same case and to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: Weakening that goes back is returned as is. Weakening that does not go back is not appraised for a thief.

steps.title: But according to אביי, the contradiction comes back
steps.stepSummary: אביי holds that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר spoke even about weakening that does not go back. So the split used for רבא does not work for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to אביי, who said that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר spoke even about weakening that does not go back, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to אביי and asks how he would deal with the contradiction in שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule covers weakening that does not go back too. So if שמואל rules like him, he would let a thief return the item as is even there. That clashes directly with 'we do not appraise for a thief.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'But according to אביי…' This switches to the view that has the problem.
What can be said? The challenge remains open.
That does not go back, meaning irreversible.

phrases.english: But according to Abaye, who said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר –
phrases.english: when Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said it,
he said it even about weakening that does not go back,
what can be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 32 works only for רבא and leaves אביי with the problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר together with שמואל's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי שמעון בן אלעזר covers weakening that does not go back, then ruling like him clashes with 'we do not appraise for a thief.'

steps.title: אביי had a different version of שמואל's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer for אביי. He learned שמואל's ruling in a different form, which the גמרא is about to quote.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי taught it like this: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא says אביי had a different version of שמואל's statement, and the actual wording comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer here does not split the cases. It changes what שמואל said: in אביי's version, שמואל did not say the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in a way that clashes. The content of that version continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught it like this. He learned a different version of the statement.

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence stops at 'שמואל said:'. The words of אביי's version come in the next part of the daf, so do not look for them here.

phrases.english: Abaye taught it like this:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: This is the same chain of names as the ruling in step 30, but אביי quotes different words, which come next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to answer the challenge of step 33 by changing the wording of שמואל's ruling for אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different version of the quoted statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone learned שמואל's ruling as 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.'
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי had a different wording of שמואל's statement, which continues in the next part of the daf.
